provenance.note: Curated compilation. Page numbers are PDF pages unless marked printed.

note: Jaipur's lake record is mostly a court record. Mansagar was restored by JDA under the National Lake Conservation Plan and its shore leased to a private developer, a lease the Supreme Court cut to 30 years in 2014; in 2025 the Court found the lake damaged again and ordered a NEERI study. Ramgarh, once the city's reservoir, has been the subject of High Court orders on its catchment since 2004 and is still empty. Where a figure rests on a party's submission rather than a finding, the text says so.

projects.scheme_name: Mansagar lake restoration (National Lake Conservation Plan)
projects.financier: Government of India 70%, Government of Rajasthan 30%
projects.scope: Restoration of Mansagar after the walled city's Nagtalai and Brahmapuri sewage drains had emptied into it since 1962: the Brahmapuri sewage plant was revamped to send treated water to the lake to make up evaporation, a two-step tertiary treatment plant was built, and the lake was cleared of hyacinth (Supreme Court 2014, PDF pp.8 and 25).
projects.funding_summary: Estimated Rs 24.72 crore; the Ministry of Environment and Forests gave administrative approval on 5 September 2002, revised on 23 December 2002 (PDF p.25). The judgment records this as the PIL petitioner's account; it gives no completion date or final cost.

projects.scheme_name: Jal Mahal precinct lease (Mansagar Lake Precincts)
projects.operator: Jal Mahal Resorts Pvt Ltd, lessee of the Government of Rajasthan
projects.scope: A 100-acre precinct on the lake shore leased on 22 November 2005 for restoring the Jal Mahal monument and building a tourism project. The Rajasthan High Court declared the lease void on 17 May 2012; on 25 April 2014 the Supreme Court reinstated it but cut the term from 99 years to 30, counted from the judgment, returned 8.65 acres to the lake, and kept 14.15 acres as a construction-free public promenade (PDF pp.143-149). It also held that a Mansagar restoration by the State or the Environment Ministry would not be affected by the lease (PDF p.147).
projects.funding_summary: Private investment; the record we hold gives no project cost. The Court was told that phase I had been complete since February 2011 (PDF p.146).
projects.status: Lease runs to April 2044 (30 years from 25 April 2014)

projects.scheme_name: Jal Mahal lake pollution control and restoration study (NEERI)
projects.operator: Nagar Nigam Heritage Jaipur, on the Supreme Court's direction
projects.scope: The Supreme Court directed the corporation to appoint NEERI within a week to report on stopping the lake's pollution and on long-term restoration; the State's development plan in its letter of 26 November 2024 may not proceed without the Court's leave until NEERI reports; no vending or market near the lake, and dumping to stop at once.
projects.status: Ordered 28 February 2025; NEERI report not found

projects.scheme_name: Ramgarh dam catchment clearing (High Court suo motu)
projects.operator: State of Rajasthan: District Collectors of Jaipur and Kotputli-Behror, Water Resources Department, JDA
projects.scope: Removal of encroachments and obstructions across Ramgarh's catchment of about 769 sq km in Andhi, Jamwa Ramgarh, Amer, Shahpura and Viratnagar tehsils, so the Banganga, Madhoveni, Roda, Gomti and Tala can reach the dam again. The State prepared an Initial Action Plan in July 2012 and a Technical Committee reported on 9 January 2013 (Supreme Court 2017, PDF p.7). On 30 July 2026 the High Court told WRD to remove all anicuts in the way of the flow and asked what had been done since 2013; on 13 August 2026 it ordered the Collector's list of encroachers published in Rajasthan Patrika and Dainik Bhaskar, with removal at the encroachers' cost.
projects.funding_summary: No budget in the court record we hold.
projects.status: Under court monitoring; dam empty on 8 October 2026

projects.scheme_name: Talkatora desilting and 1 MLD sewage plant (AMRUT)
projects.scope: One package: sewage treatment plants at Brahmapuri (8 MLD) and Tal Katora (1 MLD) on the hybrid annuity model with 15 years' operation, desilting of Tal Katora lake, and rehabilitation of the Brahmapuri outfall sewer.
projects.funding_summary: Estimated Rs 30.82 crore for the whole package; bids open 7 February to 27 March 2017; 24 months to complete.
projects.status: Tendered 2017; award and completion not found

projects.scope: The Dravyavati River Project: channel, embankments and five sewage plants along about 47.5 km of the river through the city, with ten years of operation and maintenance. No channel was built in the submergence areas of the Sikar, Gular and Ramchandrapura dams (High Court order of 19 December 2024). On 23 July 2026 the High Court asked JDA to explain why it has not built the drain channels near Ambawadi that a NEERI report recommends (D.B. CWP 2905/2024).
projects.funding_summary: Contract of 18 March 2016 with the TPL-SUCG consortium: Rs 1,470.85 crore to build and Rs 206.08 crore for ten years of operation and maintenance. JDA issued a commissioning certificate on 9 December 2022 (Rajasthan High Court, S.B. CWP 14997/2024, order of 19 December 2024).
projects.status: Commissioned 9 December 2022; three dam stretches unbuilt; court-monitored upkeep (order of 23 July 2026)

projects.scheme_name: Renovation of traditional water bodies, Jaipur district
projects.scope: A Rajya Sabha answer, republished on the open data platform, counts 405 renovations of traditional water bodies in Jaipur district between 22 March 2025 and 12 March 2026. It does not name the scheme or list the water bodies, and it counts works, not distinct water bodies.

court_orders.case: Abdul Rahman v. State of Rajasthan
court_orders.ruling: issued directions to keep water flowing in the catchments of Ramgarh dam and of the Tala and Banganga rivers, in a public interest case on protecting Rajasthan's tanks and ponds as part of the right to life under Article 21. The order of 18 July 2003 in the same case required a survey of the catchment land misused for construction. Text as recounted by the Supreme Court in 2017; the High Court's own judgment was not read.
court_orders.concern: construction and encroachment in the catchment of Ramgarh dam

court_orders.case: Suo Motu v. State of Rajasthan, with Pyar Singh Meena, Raj Kumar Meena, and Suo Motu: In the matter of Save the Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
court_orders.ruling: Opened as a single-judge suo motu case in 2011, which appointed a monitoring committee on 23 August 2011 and gave final directions on 29 May 2012. On 30 July 2026 a Division Bench directed WRD to remove all anicuts in the way of the flow to Ramgarh lake and the State to clear obstructions on five rivers. On 13 August 2026 it ordered the list of catchment encroachers published in two Hindi newspapers as statutory notice, with removal at their cost and police help if needed, and allowed citizens and journalists to report encroachments to the Jaipur Collector. Next listed 15 September 2026.
court_orders.concern: encroachments and anicuts in Ramgarh dam's catchment and on the lake bed

court_orders.case: National Institute of Medical Science University v. State of Rajasthan
court_orders.ruling: dismissed NIMS's petitions with costs of Rs 10 lakh each for 'brazen encroachment' on Khasra No. 526 in Ramgarh's catchment, and ordered JDA, with the State and the Jaipur Collector, to demolish that construction by 30 November 2017 at NIMS's expense. It recorded that the lake was still dry and that nothing substantive had been achieved on the ground despite the High Court's orders.
court_orders.concern: a university's construction in Ramgarh dam's catchment

court_orders.case: Jal Mahal Resorts P. Ltd v. K.P. Sharma and others
court_orders.ruling: partly allowed the developer's appeals against the Rajasthan High Court's judgment of 17 May 2012, which had declared the Mansagar precinct lease void. The lease stands for 30 years from the judgment instead of 99; 8.65 acres return to the State to be added to the lake; 14.15 acres stay a construction-free public promenade; a State or Environment Ministry restoration of Mansagar is not affected by the lease.
court_orders.concern: the lease of 100 acres of the lake's shore and bed to a private developer

court_orders.case: Rajender Tiwari v. Union of India and others
court_orders.court: National Green Tribunal, Central Zone Bench, Bhopal
court_orders.ruling: held Nagar Nigam Jaipur Heritage liable for environmental compensation of Rs 10,000 a day for the night market it ran beside Jal Mahal lake, inside the Nahargarh sanctuary's eco-sensitive zone, from 1 November 2022 to 24 July 2023 without the monitoring committee's permission, to be deposited with the PCCF Wildlife, Jaipur; no such market without that committee's consent.
court_orders.concern: a night market and untreated waste beside Jal Mahal lake

court_orders.case: Nagar Nigam Heritage Jaipur v. Rajendra Tiwari
court_orders.ruling: on the corporation's appeal against the NGT, recorded a forest officer's report of 20 June 2023 that the lake 'has been completely damaged' by the night market, sewage from the corporation's headquarters and waste from its Indira Rasoi scheme; directed the corporation to appoint NEERI within a week; held the State's planned development of the lake until NEERI reports; barred vending and markets near the lake. Listed 24 March 2025; later orders not found.
court_orders.concern: pollution of Jal Mahal lake by the municipal corporation

court_orders.case: Alok Gupta v. State of Rajasthan and others
court_orders.ruling: asked JDA to explain why it has not built the concrete drain channels near Ambawadi and between the hills and the Shastri Nagar to Vidyadhar Nagar road that a NEERI report recommends for the Dravyavati; listed with D.B. CWP 9497/2007 on 12 August 2026.
court_orders.concern: unbuilt drain channels on the Dravyavati
